q: Which statement best describes the relationship between a class and an object?
options: A class is an instance of an object
A class is a blueprint; an object is an instance created from that blueprint
A class and an object are the same thing in Java
An object can exist without any class
explain: A class defines attributes and methods (the blueprint). new Product(...) creates an object (an instance) that has its own copy of the instance attributes.

q: Encapsulation in Java is mainly achieved by...
options: Declaring attributes private and exposing them through public getter/setter methods
Putting all code inside the main method
explain: Encapsulation hides the internal state (private attributes) and controls access through methods, so the class can validate changes (e.g. a setter that rejects a negative price).

q: Which of these is method OVERLOADING?
options: A subclass re-implements a parent method with the same signature
Two methods in the same class with the same name but different parameter lists
explain: Overloading = same name, different parameters (compile-time polymorphism). Overriding = a subclass provides a new implementation of an inherited method with the same signature (runtime polymorphism).

q: Which statement about abstract classes and interfaces is TRUE?
options: An interface can have a constructor
An abstract class can have constructors and instance attributes, while interface attributes are implicitly public static final
A class can extend two abstract classes
Abstract classes cannot contain any implemented methods
explain: Abstract classes can hold state, constructors and concrete methods. Interface fields are constants (public static final). A class extends only ONE class but can implement MANY interfaces.

q: What does super(name) do inside a constructor?
options: Calls a static method named super
Calls the parent class (Employee) constructor - it must be the first statement
Creates a new Employee object separate from this Cashier
Calls the toString() of the parent
explain: super(...) runs the parent's constructor to initialise the inherited part of the object. If you write it, it must be the first statement; otherwise Java inserts super() automatically.

q: What happens when this code is compiled?
options: Compile error: Shape is abstract; cannot be instantiated
explain: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated with new. Create an object of a concrete subclass instead, e.g. Shape s = new Circle(2);

q: A Cashier IS-A Employee, while a Store HAS-A list of Products. These relationships are...
explain: Inheritance models IS-A (class Cashier extends Employee). Composition models HAS-A (class Store { ArrayList<Product> products; }).

q: Which keyword stops a method from being overridden by subclasses?
explain: A final method cannot be overridden; a final class cannot be extended; a final variable cannot be reassigned. abstract is the opposite: it must be overridden.

q: What is the main difference between an array and an ArrayList?
options: An array has a fixed size; an ArrayList grows and shrinks automatically
ArrayList elements cannot be accessed by index
Arrays are slower than ArrayList for get(i)
explain: int[] a = new int[5] can never hold a 6th element. An ArrayList resizes itself when you add/remove. Arrays use a.length, ArrayList uses list.size().

q: Why does ArrayList<int> numbers = new ArrayList<>(); not compile?
options: ArrayList must be given an initial size
Generics only accept reference types - use the wrapper class Integer
ArrayList needs to be imported twice
explain: Type arguments must be objects: ArrayList<Integer>, ArrayList<Double>, ArrayList<Character>... Autoboxing converts int <-> Integer for you.

q: What is printed?
explain: remove(int) removes by INDEX, so index 1 (the value 20) is removed. To remove the value 10 use list.remove(Integer.valueOf(10)).

q: Which ArrayList method REPLACES the element at a given index?
explain: set(i, v) replaces (used in Update). add(i, v) inserts and shifts the following elements to the right.

explain: add(1, "X") inserts at index 1 and shifts B and C right, so the size becomes 4.

q: What happens when you remove elements inside a for-each loop over the same ArrayList?
options: It usually throws ConcurrentModificationException - use an Iterator's remove() or removeIf instead
explain: Modifying a list while a for-each iterator walks it breaks the iterator. Use products.removeIf(p -> p.getStock() == 0) or Iterator.remove().

q: Stack and Queue order their elements as...
options: Stack = LIFO (last in, first out), Queue = FIFO (first in, first out)
explain: Stack: push/pop/peek work on the top (like an undo history). Queue: offer adds at the back, poll removes from the front (like a cashier line).

explain: Keys in a Map are unique. put with an existing key replaces the old value (and returns it).

q: Which collection automatically rejects duplicate elements?
explain: A Set never contains duplicates; set.add(x) returns false if x is already there. HashSet has no defined order, TreeSet keeps elements sorted.

q: Compared with LinkedList, ArrayList is better for...
options: Inserting/removing at the front very often
explain: ArrayList is backed by an array, so get(i) is O(1). LinkedList is better for frequent insert/remove at the ends (it also implements Queue/Deque).

q: Which modifier makes a member visible ONLY inside its own class?
explain: private = same class only. default = same package. protected = same package + subclasses. public = everywhere.

q: A member declared WITHOUT any access modifier (default / package-private) can be accessed from...
explain: Default access is package-private: every class in the same package can use it, classes in other packages cannot (even subclasses).

q: A protected attribute is accessible from...
options: The same package and subclasses (even in other packages)
explain: protected widens default access with subclasses - that is why parent attributes in inheritance exercises are often protected.

q: What happens when Main contains acc.balance = 100;?
options: Compile error: balance has private access in Account
It compiles but the value is ignored
explain: Private members are checked at compile time. Add a public method such as deposit(double amount) or setBalance(...) to Account instead.

q: Which modifier is NOT allowed on a top-level class?
explain: A top-level class can only be public or package-private (it can also be final/abstract). private/protected are allowed only on nested classes. Only one public class per file, and the file name must match it.

q: What happens when this code is compiled?
options: Compile error: attempting to assign weaker access privileges; was public
Runtime error when show() is called
explain: An overriding method can keep or widen the access level, never reduce it. The same rule makes 'void draw()' fail when implementing an interface method - interface methods are public.

q: Why does a Singleton class declare its constructor private?
options: So other classes cannot call new Database() - they must use getInstance()
explain: With a private constructor only code inside the class can create objects, so the class controls how many instances exist.

q: Order the access levels from MOST to LEAST accessible.
explain: public (everywhere) > protected (package + subclasses) > default (package) > private (class only).
